FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- CORRECTION TO MY OWN DIAGNOSIS. The remedy I gave you stands; the MECHANISM I gave you was wrong, and a wrong mechanism sends you looking in the wrong place.

WHAT I SAID: "the lexicon's proto-root walk consumes draws in registration order, so inserting a new kind into the middle shifts every draw after it -- your four additions did not append four names, they re-dealt the whole hand from the insertion point."

WHY THAT IS WRONG, and the evidence was in your own failure output. If the hand were re-dealt from an insertion point, MANY peoples would have moved. Exactly one did. Nathan flagged the mismatch; I had asserted the mechanism instead of checking it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING. `proto_root(seed, species, concept, ph)` derives from a stream keyed by the SPECIES and the CONCEPT:

  seed.derive(ROOT).derive(dynamic(species)).derive(LEXICON)
      .derive(PROTO_ROOT).derive(dynamic(concept))

That is order-INDEPENDENT. Adding duergar cannot move gully dwarf's base draw. What IS order-dependent is the next step: `assign_proto_roots` makes the family's roots INJECTIVE, and per etymology.rs:487-491 it is "collision-resolved ... on collision re-draws from a probe-keyed sub-stream". So when two kinds land on the same root, one of them re-draws -- and which one depends on assignment order.

Your duergar's base root collided with gully dwarf's `Dazha`, and the resolver moved the INCUMBENT. That is why exactly one people shifted, and why hill dwarf kept `Dashav` and desert dwarf kept `Bazap` -- they never collided. It also explains why Dazha/Dazhaf/Dashav look alike: they share the dwarf family's proto-phonology, so collisions inside that family are likelier than across it.

WHY THE REMEDY IS UNCHANGED, and now for a stated reason rather than my invented one. accession.rs:19 says: "Add a new `&[...]` to the end of EPOCH_COHORTS. **Never edit an existing one**", and the module states the guarantee outright -- "a later cohort is defined not to disturb" the earlier ones. That IS the incumbent-stability rule. Put your four kinds in a NEW cohort appended to the end, and the collision resolver leaves `Dazha` with the gully dwarfs and makes your duergars re-draw. Put them in cohort 0 and resolution order decides, which is what just happened.

SO THE CHECK IS SHARPER THAN I FIRST TOLD YOU: not "are the draws shifting" but "is `duergar` in a new appended cohort or inside an existing one". One is a rename of a committed people; the other is free.

AND ONE THING TO CARRY BEYOND THIS FIX: the resolver moving the incumbent rather than the newcomer is worth a look on its own terms, independently of cohorts. If a same-cohort collision can displace an established name, that is a sharp edge that will cut somebody else later. Whether it SHOULD is a question for whoever owns etymology, not for your campaign to settle -- but it is worth an idea-registry row while you have the evidence in hand.
